flags.purpose: Displays all active TCP connections and listening ports with protocol, local/foreign address, and state.
flags.security_use_case: Identify listening services and established connections during incident response.
flags.threat_detected: Unexpected listening ports, unauthorized external connections, potential backdoors.
flags.risk_if_misused: None; read-only. Process details may be limited without elevation.
flags.safe_followup: Use -b or -o to map connections to executables or PIDs; correlate with tasklist.

flags.purpose: Shows the executable responsible for each connection or listening port.
flags.security_use_case: Map network activity to actual binaries to detect malicious processes.
flags.threat_detected: Malware hosting services or making outbound C2 connections.
flags.risk_if_misused: Requires administrator privileges; slower on busy systems.
flags.safe_followup: Validate process with tasklist and file hash; inspect with Get-Process.

flags.purpose: Displays owning Process ID (PID) for each connection.
flags.security_use_case: Correlate suspicious connections to specific processes.

flags.purpose: Shows numerical IPs and ports without DNS/service name resolution for faster output.
flags.security_use_case: Quick port-focused investigation during live incidents.
flags.threat_detected: Connections on suspicious or uncommon ports used by malware.
flags.safe_followup: Investigate ports with Test-NetConnection or threat intel lookup.

flags.purpose: Filters output by protocol such as TCP or UDP.
flags.security_use_case: Focus on TCP connections typical of malware C2 traffic.
flags.threat_detected: Suspicious TCP sessions or excessive connection attempts.
flags.safe_followup: Inspect TCP settings with netsh interface tcp show global.

flags.purpose: Displays routing table and default gateway configuration.
flags.security_use_case: Detect unexpected gateway or route manipulation.
flags.safe_followup: Compare with baseline using route print.

flags.purpose: Shows protocol statistics summarizing errors and connection issues.
flags.security_use_case: Detect SYN floods, resets, or abnormal network behavior.
flags.threat_detected: High failure rates indicating network attacks or malware saturation.
flags.safe_followup: Correlate with firewall logs or packet capture.

flags.purpose: Displays Ethernet statistics like bytes sent/received and errors.
flags.security_use_case: Spot traffic spikes or abnormal broadcast traffic.
flags.threat_detected: Possible data exfiltration or ARP spoofing indicators.
flags.safe_followup: Use Get-NetAdapterStatistics for deeper interface analysis.

flags.purpose: Resolves foreign IP addresses to fully qualified domain names.
flags.security_use_case: Identify suspicious domains for threat intelligence lookup.
flags.threat_detected: Connections to malicious or unknown domains.
flags.risk_if_misused: DNS lookup latency; may leak DNS queries.
flags.safe_followup: Verify domains with nslookup or reputation services.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Lists all active TCP connections with PIDs for quick process correlation.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Identify external communications potentially linked to malware.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Maps listening ports directly to executables for rogue service detection.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Detect unauthorized services like rogue RDP/HTTP/SMB servers.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Monitors problematic connection states over time indicating exhaustion or DoS.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Spot connection flooding or rapid outbound attempts by malware.
